lessons.title: Ask first
lessons.scenario: You need a classmate's notes from Monday's lecture.

worked.prompt: Write a message asking for Monday's notes.
worked.answer: Could you send me Monday's notes? I missed the lecture and want to catch up before Friday.
why: The ask comes first, so the reader knows what you need.
The reason is short and comes after it.

change.prompt: Same message, but now you need Tuesday's notes. Which first line fits?

options: Could you send me Tuesday's notes?
I was not well on Monday and Tuesday.
accepted: Could you send me Tuesday's notes?

nearMisses.answer: I was not well on Monday and Tuesday.
nearMisses.feedback: That is the reason, not the ask. Put the ask first, then the reason.

feedback.right: Yes. The ask leads, so the reader can act at once.
feedback.wrong: Start with what you need from them.

accept: could you send me tuesday's notes

fresh.prompt: You need the lab key from the caretaker before 3 pm. Pick the best first line.

options: Could I borrow the lab key before 3 pm?
The lab is locked again today.
accepted: Could I borrow the lab key before 3 pm?

nearMisses.answer: The lab is locked again today.
nearMisses.feedback: That explains the problem but never asks. Lead with the ask.

feedback.right: Right. The caretaker knows what you need and by when.
feedback.wrong: A polite opener is fine later; the ask comes first.

accept: could i borrow the lab key before 3 pm

fresh.prompt: Write the first line of a message asking your neighbour to water your plants this weekend.

checklist: The ask is in the first line.
The reason is one short sentence.
lessons.useItToday: Before you send your next message, move the ask to the first line.

lessons.title: Steps in order
lessons.scenario: You are telling a friend how to reach the library from the bus stop.

worked.prompt: Give the directions in three steps.
worked.answer: Get off at the main gate. Walk past the canteen. The library is the second building on the left.
why: The steps follow the order your friend will walk them.

change.prompt: Now your friend starts at the canteen. Put the steps in order.

parts: Turn left at the notice board.
Enter the second building on the left.

answer: Turn left at the notice board.
Enter the second building on the left.
nearMisses.feedback: They cannot turn at the board before they leave the canteen. Start where they stand.

feedback.right: Yes. Each step starts where the last one ended.
feedback.wrong: Follow the walk from where your friend stands now.

accept: Turn left at the notice board.
Enter the second building on the left.
reject: Enter the second building on the left.
Turn left at the notice board.

fresh.prompt: Put the steps for starting the class projector in order.

nearMisses.feedback: It cannot switch on before it has power. Plug it in first.

feedback.right: Right. Power, then on, then the input.
feedback.wrong: Think about what the projector needs before each step.

fresh.prompt: Write three short steps for making a cup of tea for a guest.

checklist: The steps follow the real order.
lessons.useItToday: Next time you give directions, say one action at a time.

lessons.title: Name the detail
lessons.scenario: You are moving a study group meeting.

worked.prompt: Write a message moving today's meeting.
worked.answer: Can we move today's meeting to 5 pm? The room is booked until 4:30.
why: It names the new time in full.

change.prompt: The new place is Room 12. Fill the gap: "Can we meet in ___ at 5 pm?"

nearMisses.feedback: Say "Room 12", so nobody wonders whether 12 is a time.

feedback.right: Clear. The place is named in full.
feedback.wrong: Name the place in full, like "Room 12".

fresh.prompt: The new time is 6 in the evening. Fill the gap: "Can we move the meeting to ___?"

nearMisses.feedback: Add "pm", so nobody reads it as 6 in the morning.

feedback.right: Right. The time cannot be misread.
feedback.wrong: Write the evening time with "pm", like "6 pm".

fresh.prompt: Write one message that moves your next meeting and names the new time.

checklist: The new time or place is named in full.
lessons.useItToday: When you change a plan, name the new time or place in full.

comparison.prompt: Write a message asking someone for something you need this week.
